findings.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:31 — [P1, confidence 75] The unscoped `OR: [{ method: WorkflowMethods.SMS, scheduledDate: { lte: dayjs().toISOString() } }, { retryCount: { gt: 1 } }]` deletes any non-SMS workflow reminder once another delivery path records more than one retry, silently discarding that reminder even though this job owns SMS scheduling.

packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:184 — [P1, confidence 75] The stale read-modify-write `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` loses concurrent failures from overlapping cron invocations, leaving the stored count below the retry cutoff and scheduling the same failed SMS beyond its intended retry limit.

packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:158 — [P1, confidence 100] The `if (message?.length && message?.length > 0 && sendTo) {` gate leaves an SMS reminder with an empty rendered message or missing recipient at `retryCount` 0 forever, so every cron run reselects it and the retry-limit cleanup never stops the invalid reminder.

packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:39 — [P1; confidence 100] `retryCount: { gt: 1 }` is not scoped to `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS`, so this SMS cron deletes any non-SMS reminder whose retry count exceeds one and still returns a successful response after dropping that work.

packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:184 — [P1; confidence 100] `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` performs a stale read-modify-write, so overlapping cron invocations that both fail leave the count at one and retries never reach the `gt: 1` deletion threshold while duplicate scheduling attempts continue.

packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:158 — [P2; confidence 100] `if (message?.length && message?.length > 0 && sendTo) {` silently skips reminders with an empty rendered message or missing destination, leaves their retry count at zero, and returns `SMS scheduled`, causing the cron to report success forever while that reminder is never delivered.

goldens.comment: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also applies to the similar update in the catch block).

The deletion logic in scheduleSMSReminders.ts incorrectly deletes non-SMS workflow reminders (e.g., Email, WhatsApp) that have retryCount > 1. This occurs because the retryCount condition within the OR clause for deletion lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing it to apply to all reminder types instead of only SMS reminders, which is the intended scope of this function.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:158 — [P1, confidence 100] The `if (message?.length && message?.length > 0 && sendTo) {` gate leaves an SMS reminder with an empty rendered message or missing recipient at `retryCount` 0 forever, so every cron run reselects it and the retry-limit cleanup never stops the invalid reminder.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real logic flaw. Looking at the diff: (1) The deletion query at lines 31-44 only deletes reminders where `retryCount > 1`, (2) The selection query at lines 46-60 fetches unscheduled SMS reminders, (3) The processing logic around line 163 shows that `retryCount` is only incremented inside the `if (scheduledSMS)` else branch or in the catch block. If a reminder has an empty message or missing `sendTo`, the outer `if (message?.length && message?.length > 0 && sendTo)` condition fails, so the reminder is never processed, `retryCount` stays at 0, it's never deleted (since deletion requires `retryCount > 1`), and it will be reselected on every cron run indefinitely.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:184 — [P1; confidence 100] `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` performs a stale read-modify-write, so overlapping cron invocations that both fail leave the count at one and retries never reach the `gt: 1` deletion threshold while duplicate scheduling attempts continue.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a race condition. The code reads `reminder.retryCount` from the database at query time, then later increments it with `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1`. If two cron invocations run concurrently and both fail for the same reminder, they both read retryCount=0, both write retryCount=1, and the count never reaches >1 to trigger deletion. This is a valid stale read-modify-write bug. The fix would be to use Prisma's `increment` operation instead.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:158 — [P2; confidence 100] `if (message?.length && message?.length > 0 && sendTo) {` silently skips reminders with an empty rendered message or missing destination, leaves their retry count at zero, and returns `SMS scheduled`, causing the cron to report success forever while that reminder is never delivered.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that when `scheduledSMS` is truthy (line 175), the reminder is updated with a referenceId. When it's falsy (the new else block at lines 177-184), the retryCount is incremented. However, the finding points to line 158 which is the condition `if (message?.length && message?.length > 0 && sendTo)` - this condition exists in the original code (not shown in diff context but referenced). If this condition fails (empty message or no sendTo), the code skips the SMS scheduling entirely but doesn't increment retryCount, meaning the reminder stays at retryCount=0 forever. The deletion logic only removes reminders with retryCount > 1, so these reminders would never be cleaned up and the cron would keep trying to process them. This is a real bug in the retry logic.
